Package org.apache.juneau.http.classic.entity

Class BasicHttpEntity<SELF extends BasicHttpEntity<SELF>>

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.http.classic.entity.BasicHttpEntity<SELF>
Type Parameters:
SELF - The self type for fluent setters.
All Implemented Interfaces:
HttpEntity
Direct Known Subclasses:
ByteArrayEntity, FileEntity, ReaderEntity, SerializedEntity, StreamEntity, StringEntity
@BeanIgnore public abstract class BasicHttpEntity<SELF extends BasicHttpEntity<SELF>> extends Object implements HttpEntity
A basic HttpEntity implementation with additional features. Provides the following features:
  • Caching.
  • Fluent setters.
  • Fluent assertions.
  • Externally-supplied/dynamic content.

Immutability is expressed with the "funnel + nested Unmodifiable snapshot" paradigm: every fluent setter routes through the single protected modify(Runnable) choke-point, and each concrete leaf gets a nested X.Unmodifiable whose only behavioral override is a throwing modify(...). A leaf's unmodifiable() factory returns a point-in-time snapshot of type X.Unmodifiable; any attempt to set a property on it throws an UnsupportedOperationException.

This is a self-typed (CRTP) root: a leaf declares class StringEntity extends BasicHttpEntity<StringEntity> and inherits leaf-typed fluent setters with no covariant overrides.

Notes:
  • Beans are not thread safe unless they're marked as unmodifiable.

    • unmodifiable

      public abstract SELF unmodifiable()
      Returns an unmodifiable snapshot of this bean.

      The returned instance is a point-in-time copy of the leaf's nested Unmodifiable type; any attempt to set a property on it throws an UnsupportedOperationException. This method is idempotent: if this bean is already unmodifiable it returns itself rather than taking another snapshot. The receiver is left unchanged (and still modifiable unless it was already unmodifiable).

      Returns:
      An unmodifiable snapshot of this bean, or this bean if it is already unmodifiable.

    • equals

      public boolean equals(Object o)
      Compares the shared base content of two entities.

      This base implementation compares only the fields declared on BasicHttpEntity and deliberately accepts any BasicHttpEntity subtype so that concrete leaves can delegate to it via super.equals(...). It does not gate on the concrete leaf type; each concrete leaf overrides equals to first apply an instanceof <ThatLeaf> gate (so two unrelated leaves with equal base content are not equal) and then calls super.equals(...) to compare the inherited content. Using instanceof <ThatLeaf> (rather than getClass() ==) is what preserves the immutability invariant that bean.equals(bean.unmodifiable()) holds, since each X.Unmodifiable snapshot is a subclass of its leaf X.

      Overrides:
      equals in class Object

    • modify

      protected SELF modify(Runnable mutation)
      Single mutation funnel — the only choke-point through which all state changes on this bean flow.

      Every fluent setter routes through this method. The nested Unmodifiable snapshot overrides only this method to throw, which freezes the entire mutation surface with a single override.

      Parameters:
      mutation - The state change to apply.

      This object.

    • freeze

      protected void freeze()
      Deep-freeze hook invoked from the nested Unmodifiable constructor after the snapshot copy completes.

      Entities hold no mutable sub-beans (the content-type / content-encoding headers are immutable value objects, and the content buffer follows the copy-constructor's reference-copy behavior), so this is a documented no-op — the single throwing modify(Runnable) override on the nested Unmodifiable already freezes the entire mutation surface. A leaf that adds its own mutable sub-bean would override this method (calling super.freeze() first).
